chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Miskeen, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Recite Surah al-Haqqah frequently, for reciting it in the obligatory and recommended prayers is from belief in Allah and His Messenger, because it was revealed specifically regarding Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) and Mu'awiya, and the religion of its reciter will not be taken away or become doubtful until he meets Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْحَاقَّةِ: Surah al-Haqqah (The Inevitable/That which will surely befall), Chapter 69 of the Quran
key_terms.ع: Abbreviation for 'Alayhi al-Salam (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the virtue of reciting Surah al-Haqqah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the recitation of Surah al-Haqqah as a vital act of faith, specifically noting its revelation in the context of the rivalry between Imam Ali and Mu'awiya. This connection to the 'Ghazw al-Haqqah' (Battle of Truth) underscores the Surah's role in affirming Imam Ali's authority, ensuring that the reciter's faith remains intact until the final meeting with Allah.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. From the previous chain from al-Hassan from Muhammad b. Miskeen from ’Amru b. Shimr from Jabir from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:

Recite Surah Haqqah very often because recitation of Surah Haqqah in obligatory and recommended prayers is a sign of belief in Allah and His Prophet. It is related to Amirul Momineen (a.s.) and Muawiyah and the religion of the reciter would not remain doubtful and uncertain till he meets Allah.
